criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad Transaction definition
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo item 1 flags the Transaction definition as covering JVs, minority investments, recapitalizations, restructurings and a catch-all, beyond the Board's sale mandate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes narrowing Transaction to Change of Control
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup redefines Transaction as a Change of Control (50%+ of equity or voting power, all or substantially all assets, or a merger with loss of majority control).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains risk of fee trigger on unrelated transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo says the overbroad definition could tax the pending robotics JV and routine strategic activity at 1.75%, i.e., fee leakage on unrelated transactions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies above-market success fee rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states that effective fees for $150M-$300M deals are typically about 1.0%-1.5% and that a flat 1.75% at $220M is at or above the top of the market.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes reduced or tiered fee structure
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup proposes a declining scale of 1.50% up to $200M and 1.25% above, with a flat 1.50% fallback.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies inflated Aggregate Consideration definition
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo item 5 flags earnouts counted at maximum value and the inclusion of non-compete, consulting and employment payments in Aggregate Consideration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes excluding non-compete/consulting/employment payments
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup excludes non-competition, consulting, employment, retention and similar payments to equityholders, directors, officers and employees from Aggregate Consideration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes earnout valuation at fair value or as-paid basis
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup makes the fee on Contingent Consideration payable only if, as and when it is actually paid.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies inadequate 50% retainer credit
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the 50% retainer credit as below the 100% market standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes 100% retainer creditability
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup Section 4(c) provides for a 100% retainer credit against the Transaction Fee.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Quantifies economic impact of 50% credit
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo quantifies $450,000 of non-creditable retainer over a 12-month, $900,000 engagement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies excessive 24-month tail period
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo calls the 24-month tail off-market and gives 12 months as the standard and 18 months as the outer limit.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes reducing tail period to 12–18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup reduces the tail to 12 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies overbroad tail trigger ('otherwise known to Thorngate')
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo and comments flag 'otherwise known to Thorngate' as a category with no defined limit that could capture essentially every buyer in the sector.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes fixed written list of tail parties at termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup requires Thorngate to deliver a written Tail Party List of parties it actually contacted within 10 business days of termination.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies narrow indemnification carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags that the carve-outs cover only gross negligence and willful misconduct, and expands them to bad faith, fraud and material breach as the firm standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes adding bad faith, fraud, and/or material breach to carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup adds bad faith, fraud and material breach of the Agreement to the indemnification carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Addresses indefinite survival of indemnification
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags indefinite survival as disfavored and proposes 3 years after the later of termination or closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies improper $500,000 early termination fee
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the $500,000 early termination fee as not customary in sell-side engagements (Critical).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes deletion of early termination fee
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup deletes the termination fee entirely and preserves penalty-free termination on 30 days' notice; the comment notes such fees are not customary.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies principal transaction conflict of interest
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies Thorngate acting as principal or buyer as a fundamental conflict that puts the advisor on both sides of price and process.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes deletion or consent/safeguard requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup prohibits principal participation unless there is full disclosure, prior written Transaction Committee consent, and an independent fairness opinion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies undisclosed fee-sharing as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags undisclosed fee-sharing as creating hidden incentives, for example to favor a bidder introduced by a fee-sharing finder.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes requiring prior disclosure and consent for fee-sharing
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup requires prior written disclosure to, and prior written consent of, the Company for any fee-sharing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies absence of aggregate expense cap
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo item 10 notes there is no aggregate expense cap and that small items accumulate even with the $5,000 per-item approval threshold.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes aggregate expense cap
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup sets a $75,000 aggregate expense cap, with any excess requiring CFO prior written approval.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies unauthorized use of name and logo
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the perpetual licence to use the Company's name and logo without review as a confidentiality risk.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes prior approval requirement for name/logo use
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup requires prior written consent for any use of the name or logo, except post-closing tombstones, which remain subject to Company review and approval.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies financing fee as inappropriate in sell-side letter
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the 1.0% Financing Fee as inappropriate because no financing mandate was given, which would make the fee a windfall.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes deletion or separate agreement for financing fee
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup deletes the Financing Fee and makes any financing engagement subject to a separate written agreement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Identifies liability cap as overly protective of advisor
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags that the cap at fees received is one-way and advisor-favorable, and could limit exposure to about $150,000 even for a confidentiality breach or fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Proposes carve-outs from liability cap or deletion
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup carves fraud, bad faith, willful misconduct, gross negligence, and breaches of the confidentiality and conflicts sections out of the liability cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Identifies Washington DC arbitration venue as disadvantageous
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the DC seat as Thorngate's home city, while the governing law is New York and the Company is in Michigan.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Proposes New York as arbitration venue
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup moves the arbitration seat to New York, New York, with Michigan as the fallback.

criteria_results.title: Memo includes priority ranking for each issue
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo assigns Critical, Important or Minor to every one of its 26 issues and includes a priority summary appendix.

criteria_results.title: Memo notes provisions that are market-standard and acceptable
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo Part VI lists the market-standard provisions it accepts, including the $75,000 retainer, the 30-day notice period, AAA arbitration and New York law.

criteria_results.title: Markup includes bracketed comments explaining substantive changes
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup contains margin comments by Ledgerwood & Pratt explaining the rationale for each substantive revision.

criteria_results.title: Deliverable: Redlined/marked-up engagement letter produced
criteria_results.reasoning: A redlined/marked-up engagement letter (engagement-letter-markup.docx) is produced as a separate deliverable.

criteria_results.title: Deliverable: Commentary memo produced
criteria_results.reasoning: A separate commentary memo (markup-commentary-memo.docx) is produced.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Voss Dynamics as the client throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: Both deliverables consistently treat Voss Dynamics Inc. as the client and Thorngate Partners LLC as the advisor/counterparty.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Tail applies regardless of who introduced counterparty flagged
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo and comments flag the 'regardless of who introduced' language, which would capture buyers who approach the Company independently, and delete it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Flags 'finally judicially determined' standard as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo item 15 addresses the 'finally judicially determined by a court' standard, noting that because disputes go to arbitration a judicial determination may never occur, which makes the carve-outs illusory.
